moat_against: No pricing power — premiums are filed a year in advance and the ACA 80% minimum MLR caps underwriting margin by law; pricing errors (FY2025) cannot be corrected in-year
Risk adjustment structurally taxes its exact franchise — a younger/healthier pool pays net transfers of ~18.5% of direct premiums (FY2025), and late CMS true-ups blew MLR out to 87.4% in FY2025

No switching costs and single-market concentration — annual open enrollment churn, essentially all revenue from ACA individual/small-group, exposed to enhanced-subsidy expiry and CMS program-integrity disenrollment (up to ~300k members flagged)

No through-cycle earnings record — operating losses in 2019–2023 and FY2025; ROIC history (where measurable) is negative-to-thin, and much larger rivals (UNH, CVS, Centene, Molina) carry bigger scale and diversified earnings
moat_for: Administrative cost edge — proprietary tech/AI claims and servicing platform cut the SG&A ratio from 19.1% (FY2024) to 17.5% (FY2025), guided 15.6–16.1% FY2026, record-low 14.2% in Q2 2026
Exchange scale — 2.96M members at 2026-06-30 (+46% YoY), one of the largest pure-play ACA carriers, gaining share as larger rivals retreat from the exchanges
Member-experience brand and engagement in the individual market, plus ICHRA/+Oscar platform optionality beyond its own risk book
moat_justification: Weak moat: a technology-led ACA exchange insurer whose genuine edge is administrative cost — SG&A ratio fell from 19.1% of revenue (FY2024) to 17.5% (FY2025) to a guided 15.6–16.1% for FY2026, with a record-low 14.2% in Q2 2026 — plus scale as one of the largest pure-play exchange carriers (2.96M members at 2026-06-30, +46% YoY). But there is no pricing power (rates are filed a year ahead and the ACA's 80% minimum MLR caps underwriting margin by law), no switching costs (annual open enrollment, members churn freely), and its young/healthy member mix is structurally taxed by risk adjustment (net risk-adjustment transfer ~18.5% of direct premiums in FY2025). The measured earnings history argues against a wide moat: operating income was negative in every year 2019–2023 and again in FY2025 (-$396,357,000), with only FY2024 (+$57,265,000) and the TTM to 2026-06-30 (+$629,723,000, fundamentals.json) positive; fundamentals.json's roic_proxy series is not meaningful here because the denominator (equity + debt - cash) is negative at a net-cash insurer, so operating margin and MLR are the usable evidence — MLR 81.7% (FY2024) blew out to 87.4% (FY2025) before the guided 81–82% for FY2026, i.e. underwriting results are set by market morbidity and CMS risk adjustment, not by Oscar.
name: Oscar Health, Inc.
one_liner: ACA health insurer in a real 2026 earnings inflection, moat 3/10 — engine prints Tier C (weighted IRR 12.13%, IV@15% $24.88 vs $32.35) on an OCF base that capitalizes premium float, so the final tier is softened to D at low confidence; on accrual earnings the last-3 median base is negative, and it clears 15% only below ~$24.88 even on engine numbers.
sector: Health Care / Health Plans (ACA individual-market insurer)
tier_override_reason: SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH insurer artifact (the universe classifies OSCR as Health Care — SIC 6324 Hospital & Medical Service Plans — so the engine's Finance/Real Estate/Utilities flag did not fire, but economically this is an insurer): the OCF-based OE base capitalizes premium float and claims/risk-adjustment working capital. FY2025 conservative OE is $970,828,000 against a net loss of -$443,151,000 (financials_history.csv), and TTM OE of $4,304,752,000 (ttm.json) is ~7.8x TTM net income of $550,743,000 (fundamentals.json TTM to 2026-06-30). A payable-earnings (accrual) base built only from financials_history.csv figures — net income + D&A - capex per share, SBC already expensed inside net income so not deducted twice — is -$1.20 (2023: -270,728,000 + 30,694,000 - 25,577,000 over 221,655,000 shares), +$0.11 (2024: 25,432,000 + 32,145,000 - 27,897,000 over 265,853,000) and -$1.72 (2025: -443,151,000 + 28,892,000 - 36,372,000 over 262,388,000), a last-3 median of -$1.20/share against the engine's +$3.16 OCF base. The engine base also divides by the loss-year FY2025 diluted count of 262,388,000 while the profitable H1 2026 diluted count is 331,292,000 (ttm.json), overstating per-share OE by ~26% on the current diluted basis. Softened one notch C to D under the standing insurer-float policy (Andrew, 2026-10-15), confidence low — same treatment as PFG/HIG/ACGL/WRB.
